paper_title: Shining Light on the Dark Sector: Search for Axion-like Particles and Other New Physics in Photonic Final States with FASER
notes: FASER first search for a light long-lived particle decaying to two photons (2022-2023 pp data, 57.7/fb, 13.6 TeV). Headline result is the ALP-W model (ALP coupling to SU(2)_L gauge bosons), Lagrangian L=-(1/4) g_aWW a W W-tilde, world-leading for m_a up to 300 MeV and g_aWW ~1e-4 GeV^-1. The task table has no g_aWW plane, so the headline ALP-W observed 90% CL exclusion (Fig.10 / Fig.17a, blue closed contour) is converted to the canonical photon coupling using the paper own a->gamma-gamma vertex g_aWW*sin^2(theta_W) (Fig.1b): g_agamma = g_aWW * sin^2(theta_W), sin^2(theta_W)=0.231. Points are the full closed excluded contour (banana/nose): lower branch traced left->right (m~60->348 MeV) then upper branch right->left back to m~86 MeV where g_aWW hits the 1e-3 axis top. Extracted by vision from raster figs/alpw_final_BW.png; x-axis 200 MeV @1523 px/decade, y-axis 1e-3@px53 447 px/decade. Native g_aWW range ~1.9e-5 (nose tip m~348 MeV) to 1e-3 (m~86 MeV); e.g. lower-edge best g_aWW~1.85e-5 at m~300-320 MeV, consistent with abstract (300 MeV excluded at 2e-5 GeV^-1). Not a DM search (collider LLP), so density-independent. The paper also gives a native ALP-photon g_agamma limit (Fig.11 left/17b, m up to ~90 MeV, g down to ~1e-4, entirely within existing NA64/E137 limits) - NOT reported here since ALP-W is the headline; if the compilation instead uses that curve, this report would differ. Confidence reduced by ambiguity in whether the maintainer stored native g_aWW vs converted g_agamma.
